title: SEBI Lets REITs and InvITs Issue Depository Receipts to Draw Foreign Investment
court: Securities and Exchange Board of India
case_name: SEBI circular permitting REITs and InvITs to issue depository receipts to foreign investors
citation: Circular No. HO/17/11/19(7)2026-DDHS-RAC/I/24932/2026 for REITs, with a same-day companion circular for InvITs, both dated 2 November 2026
card_summary: SEBI's circular of 2 November 2026 lets REITs issue foreign currency depository receipts against their units, with a same-day companion circular doing the same for InvITs, so overseas investors can gain exposure without holding the units directly. Receipts can be issued only on International Financial Services Centre exchanges, and a large fresh issue needs a 75 percent unit holder vote.
card_tip: REIT and InvIT sponsors courting overseas capital should check the IFSC listing requirement, the unit holder vote threshold and the price parity safeguard before structuring a depository receipt issue.
verification_notes: The circular number for REITs (HO/17/11/19(7)2026-DDHS-RAC/I/24932/2026), the same-day companion circular for InvITs, the 2 November 2026 date and immediate effect, the IFSC-only listing condition, the bar on resident Indians holding the receipts and the 75 percent unit holder approval threshold for a large fresh issue are consistent across LiveLaw Biz, GK Today and New Kerala reports seen in this run. The circular text itself was not opened; the August 2026 consultation paper that preceded it (seen in TaxGuru and LiveLaw Biz coverage) was treated only as background, not as the operative instrument. Audience: this update serves foreign institutional investors and REIT/InvIT sponsors seeking foreign capital, consistent with the regional and audience focus for this batch.
